messages:
sam: Heads-up — saw a coordinated probing pattern from three tenant IDs this morning. They spin short bursts (5–15s) at varying rates and cause eviction churn in the small-pool nodes. Noticed around 03:12 UTC.

maria: Ugh. Any obvious fingerprint? same auth key or IP range?

sam: same tenant ids but they rotate source IPs. Auth looks valid, so this is probably application-level probing (clients trying many prompts/params).

lee: Do we have a metric for short-lived burst evictions? I can add a dashboard if we agree on signal.

sam: Yeah — eviction.count by node_type, plus short_window_token_rate > X and active_connections < 3. Quick log snippet:

```
2026-03-19T03:12:11Z tenant=tn-42 req_id=abc123 tokens=45 duration_ms=12 model=hippo-1 evicted=false
2026-03-19T03:12:16Z tenant=tn-42 req_id=abc124 tokens=512 duration_ms=1200 model=hippo-1 evicted=true reason=pool-pressure
2026-03-19T03:12:19Z tenant=tn-42 req_id=abc125 tokens=23 duration_ms=8 model=hippo-1 evicted=false
```

jordan: Sounds like classic probing to find model capacity. We should avoid per-tenant hard-caps that break legit bursty apps. Proposal: add an adaptive short-term throttle that tracks a 30s window + an "probe score" that increments on high variance in token rate and quick evictions. If score>threshold, apply graduated penalties (delay, token-reduction, deny).

maria: I like graduated penalties. How do we avoid punishing apps with genuine spiky workloads (e.g., chatbots during a flash event)?

jordan: Two levers: (1) long-term baseline — 24h avg usage — gives headroom; (2) behavior heuristics — repeated small-request bursts spaced <5s is suspicious. Also keep fast fallback to dedicated queue for customers with reserved capacity.

lee: Implementation-wise: do we want this in the ingress side (edge) or inside the scheduler? Edge gives fast rejects, scheduler gives better context for eviction decisions.

sam: Edge + token: edge emits a "probing_hint" header when local heuristics spike; scheduler consumes hints to bias admission and eviction. That keeps UX snappy and avoids cross-service chase.

maria: How about configuration surface? We need operator-friendly knobs per-tenant: probe_sensitivity, burst_window_s, penalty_tiers. Ideally default safe values and an opt-out for enterprise customers.

jordan: Agreed. Also need observability: per-tenant probe_score time-series, penalty_applied bool, and outcome (served/delayed/evicted).

lee: Quick sketch of policy proto: 
```
message ProbePolicy {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  int32 burst_window_s = 2;          // e.g., 30
  double probe_threshold = 3.5;      // score above which penalties start
  repeated PenaltyTier tiers = 4;    // mapping score -> action
}
```

sam: For penalties: start with a tiny jittered delay (100-500ms), escalate to rate-multiplier (0.5x tokens) and finally to short deny (2–10s). We should avoid permanent bans unless abuse_score persists over hours.

maria: What about false positives due to multi-instance clients (e.g., many legit clients behind a single tenant)? Could look at distinct user-agent or session token entropy.

jordan: Good call — add session_fingerprint_entropy as a signal. Also consider a cooldown reset if we see consistent success (no evictions) for a rolling 5m window.

lee: Any infra risk? We will need a small state store per-tenant for sliding windows. Could use Redis with local LRU cache on ingress nodes to avoid RPS to central store.

sam: Yep. Plan: local cache for hot tenants + periodic sync to global store for persistent stats. Keep the state small: counters and last-change timestamp.

maria: Ops playbook: when penalty hits, page infra-team only if penalty persists >30m or if multiple tenants spike together. For tenants that are paying, SRE should contact account team earlier.

jordan: We should run an internal canary: enable probe-detection in read-only mode (emit events but don't apply penalties) for 48h, review false-positive rate, then flip to graduated enforcement in a week.

sam: I'll open a follow-up RFC with metrics, proto, and rollout plan. Short-term action: lee, can you add eviction + short_window_rate dashboard panels? maria, can you draft the canary experiment steps?

lee: Will do — adding panels this afternoon.

maria: On it, will draft canary and opt-out flow.

infra-bot: Deployed alert rule draft to staging: rule/tenant-probe-spike. Trigger threshold = 4.5 probe_score. (deployment 2026-03-19T10:05:00Z) :white_check_mark:
